title.narrative: From Seed to Tempeh: Building an Inclusive Soy Value Chain in India

description.narrative: The project “From Seed to Tempeh: an inclusive and sustainable soy value chain in India” addresses critical social and environmental challenges in soybean production in Maharashtra, India. Currently, smallholder soy farmers operate under difficult conditions: incomes are low and unstable, production is heavily dependent on rain and chemical inputs, and farmers have limited access to quality seeds, knowledge, and markets. Their weak position in the value chain, selling mainly through intermediaries, reduces their bargaining power and prevents them from capturing fair value. These challenges are particularly severe for marginalized groups, including persons with disabilities and people affected by leprosy, who face discrimination and limited livelihood opportunities. The project directly benefits approximately 1,000 smallholder farmers, as well as vulnerable households involved in local processing and tempeh production. Additional beneficiaries include marginalized workers in a new soy processing facility and families engaged in Micro Fermentation Units (MFUs), enabling community-based tempeh production. Special attention is given to socially excluded groups, aiming for their full and equitable participation in the value chain. Through an integrated approach, the project seeks to transform the soy-to-tempeh value chain. Key interventions include farmer training in sustainable and regenerative agriculture, establishment of a farmer organisation, development of local processing and storage facilities, and introduction of traceability systems. These measures will improve productivity, reduce environmental impact, and strengthen farmers’ market position.The envisioned impact is a more inclusive, resilient, and environmentally responsible value chain. Farmers will achieve higher and more stable incomes, working conditions will improve, and environmental risks, such as soil degradation and pesticide use, will be reduced. At the same time, the project enhances supply chain transparency and ensures a reliable, high-quality source of soy for sustainable tempeh production
